items.q: How many UNESCO World Heritage sites are there in Berlin?
items.a: **Three properties, spread over about ten places you can actually visit.** Museum Island was listed in 1999. The Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin were listed in 1990 and include Schloss Glienicke and the Pfaueninsel on the Berlin side. The Berlin Modernism Housing Estates were listed in 2008 with six estates and extended to seven on 26 July 2026.

items.q: What was added to the Berlin World Heritage list in 2026?
items.a: **The Waldsiedlung Zehlendorf, known as Onkel Toms Hütte.** The UNESCO World Heritage Committee approved it at its 48th session in Busan on 26 July 2026, making it the seventh Berlin Modernism estate. Bruno Taut, Hugo Häring and Otto Rudolf Salvisberg built 1,917 homes there between 1926 and 1932, and the U3 station sits inside the estate.

items.q: Which Berlin World Heritage site is worth visiting if I only have a couple of hours?
items.a: **Museum Island, and after that the Hufeisensiedlung in Britz.** Museum Island is three minutes from Alexanderplatz on the U5, so the journey costs you nothing. The Hufeisensiedlung is twenty-two minutes on the U7 to Parchimer Allee and gives you a real shape to walk, which most of the other estates do not.

items.q: Can you go inside the Berlin Modernism Housing Estates?
items.a: **No, they are lived-in flats and houses, not museums.** You walk the public streets and courtyards, which is genuinely what the architecture was designed to be read from. The exception is the Hufeisensiedlung, where residents run guided tours and one Bruno Taut house is furnished in 1920s style and let to guests.

items.q: Do I need a special ticket to reach Berlin's World Heritage sites?
items.a: **No. Every one of them is inside the Berlin city boundary, so a normal AB ticket covers the journey.** The estates and the parks cost nothing to walk. Schloss Glienicke charges 8.00 EUR, reduced 6.00 EUR, and the Pfaueninsel ferry is 6.00 EUR, reduced 5.00 EUR, with the palace another 8.00 EUR on top.

items.q: Is Museum Island still worth it while the Pergamonmuseum is closed?
items.a: **Yes, four of the five museums are open and the ensemble itself is the listed thing.** The Pergamonmuseum is closed for rebuilding and reopens on 4 June 2027. The Altes Museum, Neues Museum, Alte Nationalgalerie and Bode-Museum are all working normally in the meantime.

items.q: Is Sanssouci in Potsdam part of Berlin's World Heritage?
items.a: **It is part of the same property, but it is in Potsdam, not Berlin.** The listing is called Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin, and the Berlin components are Schloss Glienicke and the Pfaueninsel out at Wannsee. Sanssouci needs its own half day.
